semantic_correction.stem: Which exercise advice is consistent with current CDC fall-prevention guidance for an older adult?

options.A: Include activities that strengthen the legs and improve balance, such as appropriately selected balance exercise or Tai Chi.
options.B: Avoid regular physical activity because reducing movement is the most reliable way to prevent falls.
options.C: Focus on flexibility exercise and omit balance training because flexibility provides the main fall-prevention benefit.
options.D: Emphasize upper-body strengthening while avoiding leg-strength and balance work during fall-prevention training.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC fall-prevention guidance updated January 27, 2026 specifically recommends exercises that make the legs stronger and improve balance and identifies Tai Chi as an example. CDC physical-activity guidance for adults age 65 and older also includes muscle-strengthening and balance activities each week. Therefore option A is correct. Avoiding activity or omitting leg-strength and balance work conflicts with current fall-prevention guidance.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach older adults at risk for falls to include exercises that improve leg strength and balance as part of fall prevention.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests CDC-supported leg-strength and balance exercise for older-adult fall prevention without absolute wording cues.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches current CDC strength-and-balance fall-prevention guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC recommends appropriate physical activity rather than activity avoidance.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Balance and strengthening are specifically recommended; flexibility alone is not the tested fall-prevention strategy.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC specifically emphasizes leg strength and balance, not upper-body training alone.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone includes both exercise domains directly recommended by CDC for fall prevention.
cueing_check: All four choices are exercise plans of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
